Cycling in the French Alps

Conquer Iconic Climbs & Alpine Beauty

A CYCLIST'S DREAM

The French Alps are a cyclist’s dream, offering legendary climbs, sweeping alpine vistas, and routes steeped in cycling history. From the high passes of the Tour de France to serene alpine valleys, our French Alps cycling tours provide the perfect combination of performance riding, breathtaking landscapes, and authentic French culture. Whether you’re tackling epic cols or enjoying scenic descents, the French Alps deliver an unforgettable cycling experience.

FRENCH ALPS FACTS

LOCATION

The French Alps stretch from Morzine in the north to Nice on the Mediterranean coast, covering regions including Haute-Savoie, Savoie, Isère, and the southern Alps. Cyclists can explore alpine peaks, verdant valleys, crystal-clear lakes, and historic villages. This diversity makes it ideal for both road and gravel cycling, offering everything from epic climbs to gentle scenic rides.

CLIMATE

The French Alps offer a variety of climates depending on altitude and location. Mountain areas have cooler temperatures with mild summers, perfect for challenging climbs, while valleys and lower slopes enjoy warmer conditions. Spring and early summer provide long sunny days, ideal for riding, and autumn brings colorful foliage and quieter roads. Coastal areas near Nice offer a Mediterranean climate, making the region rideable almost year-round.

CUISINE

Cycling in the French Alps is a treat for the senses. Alpine cuisine is hearty, featuring cheeses like Reblochon and Beaufort, cured meats, fresh vegetables, and rustic mountain dishes. As you move south toward the Mediterranean, the cuisine transitions to Provençal flavors with fresh seafood, olive oil, herbs, and local wines. Local taverns and bistros provide authentic meals to fuel cyclists after a long ride.

TERRAIN

The French Alps offer one of the most varied cycling terrains in Europe: Epic alpine passes: Col de la Madeleine, Col du Galibier, Col de la Croix de Fer, Col d’Izoard Rolling valleys and foothills for endurance and recovery rides Smooth tarmac roads with light traffic outside towns Gravel and secondary roads for off-road adventure Dramatic descents from alpine heights down to the Mediterranean coast.
